stis.title: HST STIS: Czerny-Turner long-slit spectrograph behind a two-mirror corrector, off-axis elliptical collimator, MSM plane gratings (121.6-1200 /mm), 21 um 1024 x 1024 CCD; CCD first-order modes G430L, G750L, G430M, G750M

params.value: in operation since 1997 February (installed on the second servicing mission); the explorer preset represents the post-SM4 (2009) instrument documented in the Cycle 34 handbook, CCD modes
params.quote: The Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) instrument was installed on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) during the second servicing mission, in 1997 February.
params.alt: HB32 Sec. 3.2.2: "The STIS optical design includes corrective optics to compensate for HST's spherical aberration"
params.note: STIS was down from 2004 to 2009 and repaired on SM4 (HB Sec. 2.2 is not saved); the grating, slit and CCD values below do not depend on that. No '(design)' tag.

params.quote: geometric area of a filled, unobstructed, 2.4 meter aperture
params.note: The unobstructed 2.4 m is the throughput normalization; HST's central obstruction is not modeled by the explorer.

params.parameter: HST beam at the STIS entrance
params.quote: This beam slightly overfills the f/24 cone from the telescope.
params.note: The calibration beam is built to mimic the telescope's cone at the slit wheel; the handbook states no focal ratio. That the slit wheel itself sees f/24 (the corrector re-images the HST focus 1:1) is INFERRED: W98 says the IM lamp optics deliver 'approximately the correct cone angle', and the spherical corrector mirror images the pupil, the anamorphic mirror 're-images the corrected HST image onto the spectrometer slit wheel'. The explorer's plate scale does not depend on F (see the DERIVED rows).

params.parameter: Plate scale at the slit wheel
params.value: 3.581 arcsec/mm (INFERRED, f/24 on 2.4 m)
params.note: 206265 / (2400 mm x 24) = 3.581 arcsec/mm, i.e. 1 CCD pixel (0.05078 arcsec) = 14.18 um at the slit. Used only to give the camera/collimator magnification below; not a published number.

'This "utility" slit is supported for all first-order gratings ... It provides a good compromise between spectral resolution and photometric throughput.' (A02). HB42 Sec. 4.2.2: 'The 0.2 arcsecond-wide slit is the general utility slit used most often'.

params.alt: HB42 Sec. 4.2.2: "lengths of 52 arcseconds (as projected on the CCD detector)"
params.note: The long slits are 52 arcsec; they project onto the full 1024 rows (52.0 arcsec / 0.05078 = 1024 pixels). W98 Table 7 gives 52.

params.quote: The actual width of this aperture is 34 milliarcsec instead of 50 milliarcsec
params.alt: W98 Table 7: 0.049, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 2 arcsec (52X0.05 listed at 0.049 there)
params.note: Conflict: W98 Table 7 gives 0.049 arcsec for 52X0.05, the handbook gives 0.034 (see Conflicts). 52X0.1 (HB42: 'the 0.1 arcsecond width matches the 2 pixel resolution of the CCD') is the narrowest slit that needs the explorer's slit-diffraction rule; 52X0.1 and 52X0.05 need a PEAKUP (A01, A005).
Slit-loss factor for a point source (energy passing the slit); the explorer does not model throughput.

params.parameter: Number of spectra on the detector
params.quote: long slits of widths 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 and 2.0 arcseconds
params.note: nObj = 1: one long slit, one spectrum with 1024 spatial rows (explorer convention for single-object slits). Slitless mode (R ~ 10-500 in the UV) and the 0.2X0.2 aperture are not entered.

params.value: a sphere (1st mirror, focusable over 55 mm, tilt for pupil centering) imaging the HST pupil onto an anamorphic, slightly toroidal asphere (2nd mirror) that corrects spherical aberration and astigmatism and re-images the HST focus onto the slit wheel
params.quote: The first mirror is a sphere that images the HST pupil onto the second corrector mirror, which is an anamorphic asphere that is slightly toroidal in shape.
params.alt: W98 Sec. 3: "The first is a two-element reflecting corrector, which eliminates the spherical aberration created by the primary mirror manufacturing error"; Sec. 6.3: "the first corrector mirror is independently focusable over a 55"
params.note: Drawing note only (the explorer has no corrector); the HST pupil is imaged onto CM2, which also has a hole behind the telescope-secondary shadow for the HITM lamps.

params.value: 65 apertures on four segments, at the corrected HST focal plane
params.quote: which provides 65 apertures or slits, for limiting the field
params.alt: HB32: "a telescope focal plane slit-wheel assembly"

params.value: single off-axis ELLIPTICAL mirror; OFF-AXIS (the slit is not in the returning beam)
params.quote: the light is collimated by an off-axis elliptical mirror
params.alt: Fig. 2 label "Collimation Mirror" standing to the side of the slit wheel, beam path slit wheel -> mirror -> grating wheel (MSM), read from the drawing (FIG31)
params.note: Deploy gate: off-axis, so the explorer's automatic colTilt applies (do NOT set colTilt 0). The tilt angle is NOT FOUND in the open literature (the drawing has no scale).

params.quote: to cover the 19 mm pupil diameter
params.note: The MSM optics are 25 mm in diameter 'to cover the 19 mm pupil diameter'. The collimator's focal length is NOT FOUND. DERIVED (INFERRED f/24 at the slit): f_col = 24 x 19 = 456 mm; see the effective values below, which differ.

params.value: nutating grating wheel with 21 optical elements (first-order gratings, cross-dispersers, prism, mirrors); selects the element and tilts it (scan for the M modes); sits 'near an image of the system pupil'
params.quote: is near an image of the system pupil
params.alt: HB32 Sec. 3.2.2: "It permits the selection of one of its 21 optical elements as well as adjustment of the tip and tilt angles of the selected grating or mirror."
params.note: The G430M and G750M gratings are scanned by tilting the MSM (W98 Sec. 6.1: 'all four medium-resolution long-slit modes (G140M, G230M, G430M, and G750M)'). The explorer's lamC follows the tilt at a fixed psi.

params.parameter: Spectrograph configuration of the CCD modes
params.value: Czerny-Turner: collimator -> plane grating on the MSM -> fold mirror -> camera mirror -> detector (six reflective surfaces counting the two correctors); the UV G140L and G230L are Wadsworth (parabolic gratings), not CCD modes
params.quote: Czerny-Turner spectrometers (six reflective surfaces including the corrector)
params.alt: W98 Sec. 3.2: "In the Czerny-Turner configuration, light from the collimation mirror is intercepted by either a plane grating or a prism on the grating wheel." and "The fold mirror/echelle grating directs the light toward the respective camera mirror, which focuses the dispersed energy onto the appropriate detector"
params.note: CCD first-order modes: INFERRED to use the fold-mirror branch (W98 describes the fold mirror / echelle branch as one sentence and Fig. 2 draws 'Flat Mirrors (3)' near the MAMAs; the CCD mode path to the CCD camera mirror is not drawn). The camera is a single mirror (cam 'mirror' in the explorer; 'camera mirrors' labeled K1-K3 in Fig. 2).

params.value: reflection, ruled, plane gratings in first order; 25 mm diameter
params.quote: The other 10 first-order gratings are replicated on plane grating blanks.
params.alt: W98 Sec. 3.3: "12 of which are used in first order and four of which are echelle gratings"; "grating constants ranging from 67 to 3600 grooves"
params.note: Order m = 1 for all four CCD modes (also stated in HB41 Table 4.1 'First-Order Spectroscopy').

Manufacturer Hyperfine. DERIVED Littrow blaze wavelength lamB1 = 2 sin(1.33 deg) / 121.60 mm^-1 = 2 x 0.023210 / 121.60 = 3817 A (assumes the blaze angle is the facet angle and the Littrow condition; the explorer's lamB1).
Manufacturer Milton-Roy. DERIVED lamB1 = 2 sin(1.43 deg) / 67.56 = 2 x 0.024951 / 67.56 = 7386 A.

layout.text: W98 Fig. 2 "Optical layout of STIS" (p. 1190, PDF p. 8; a perspective sketch with the lamp, mode select mechanism, slit wheel, correction mirrors, collimation mirror, camera mirrors, the four echelles, flat mirrors and the three detectors labeled; no scale bar and no dimensions) and the STIS Instrument Handbook Fig. 3.1 "Simplified STIS Optical Design" (the same drawing; saved as FIG31). Both were read as images: this record has no published dimensioned layout, no Code V file and no optical prescription. Kimble et al. 1998 (ApJ 492, L83) and the SPIE papers (Bowers et al. 1998, 3356, 401; Content et al. 1996, 2807, 267) are behind publisher bot checks or paywalls and were not obtained (NOT FOUND).

Telescope focus -> (calibration insertion mechanism, external shutter) -> first corrector mirror (sphere, W98 Sec. 3.1) -> second corrector mirror (anamorphic asphere, hole for the HITM lamps) -> slit wheel at the corrected focus -> collimation mirror (off-axis ellipse) -> mode select mechanism (MSM) with the plane grating, near a pupil image -> fold mirror -> camera mirror -> CCD (W98 Secs. 3.1-3.3 and 5-6; the Czerny-Turner branch is described in one sentence, W98 Sec. 3.2).

OFF-AXIS: "the light is collimated by an off-axis elliptical mirror" (W98 Sec. 3.2). The slit wheel is not in the returning beam (the corrected focus sits at the entrance; the collimated beam goes to the MSM). Verdict: off-axis, so the explorer's default (automatic) colTilt applies; do not enter colTilt 0. The tilt angle is NOT FOUND.

In Fig. 2 and Fig. 3.1 the slit wheel and the MSM stand side by side on the telescope end; the collimation mirror stands to the right of (beyond) the slit wheel; the camera mirrors (K1-K3, labeled) stand above the slit wheel; the CCD sits at the top of the drawing, the MAMAs and echelles at the far right on the detector bulkhead. The perspective drawing carries no scale, so no fold angle, no collimator-to-grating distance and no grating-to-camera distance can be read: layLen and camLen are NOT FOUND and the explorer's defaults draw the CCD modes schematically. The drawing is mode-independent up to the MSM ('The beam path is common up to the mode select mechanism', W98 Fig. 2 caption).

The grating wheel stands near a pupil image; the optics on it are about 25 mm across 'to cover the 19 mm pupil diameter' (W98 Sec. 3.3). The first corrector mirror images the HST pupil onto the second corrector mirror (W98 Sec. 3.1).

The camera-collimator angle psi = alpha - beta is not published. INFERRED psi = 21 deg from the anamorphic factor: W98 Table 5 gives the along-dispersion pixel 0.0512 vs 0.0507 arcsec across for G430L/G750L (factor 1.0099, which fixes psi at 21 +/- 3 deg with the model's grating equation) and then predicts, independently, the M modes' ranges: the model at psi = 21 gives 0.0545-0.0578 for G430M tilts 3165-5471 (W98 0.0543-0.0578) and 0.0542-0.0570 for G750M tilts 5734-9851 (W98 0.0540-0.0570). psi = 10 and 30 deg give 0.0525-0.0539 and 0.0565-0.0616: excluded.

atmospheric_cut.share: 180 / 2590 = 6.9 % of the complete range; the 3165 tilt (nominal 3022-3308) shows 3200-3308, losing 178 / 286 = 62 %; the 3305 secondary loses ~38 A (13 %); 3423 and redder tilts lose none
100 %: the whole mode lies below 3200 A

not_found: Kimble, R. A., Woodgate, B. E., Bowers, C. W., et al. 1998, ApJ 492, L83, "The On-Orbit Performance of the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph" (ADS 1998ApJ...492L..83K; https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/311102/pdf): the publisher link returns a Radware bot-check page, not the PDF; not downloaded. Please supply the PDF if wanted (on-orbit R, plate scales, throughputs).

Bowers, C. W., et al. 1998, SPIE 3356, 401, "On-orbit optical performance of the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph" (1998SPIE.3356..401B) and Content, R., et al. 1996, SPIE 2807, 267, "Development and testing of diffraction gratings for the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph" (1996SPIE.2807..267C): SPIE refuses automated access; no free copy found. They would give measured gratings, efficiencies and perhaps the camera geometry.

A dimensioned optical layout, the collimator's and the cameras' focal lengths, the collimator tilt, the fold-mirror angle and the collimator-grating-camera distances: not in W98, the handbook, or any free source found (STIS is a Ball Aerospace/GSFC build; the design reports are not public). The explorer's collimator focal length is therefore set from the published pupil and plate scale, EFFECTIVE (below).

The camera-collimator angle psi (INFERRED from the anamorphic plate scales instead); the CCD first-order gratings' ruled areas (gLen); the camera mirrors' focal lengths and the CCD camera's focal ratio.
The slit width used in the ground-test resolving powers of W98 Table 1 (445-770 for G430L, etc.).
The handbook's own statement of the f/ratio at the slit wheel (the handbook gives none; W98 Sec. 5 gives f/24 only for the calibration beam).

Echelle gamma (out-of-plane angle), the cross-disperser's psi and the echelle ruled lengths per mode (W98 Sec. 3.3 gives only two echelle sizes, 56 x 30 mm and 56 x 76 mm, not tied to modes): the UV echelle modes are a documentation record, not a state.
conflicts: 52X0.05 width: W98 Table 7 prints 0.049 arcsec; the handbook says "The actual width of this aperture is 34 milliarcsec instead of 50 milliarcsec" (the as-built slit measured on orbit). Preset uses 0.2 arcsec, unaffected.

Dispersions: handbook G430L 2.73, G750L 4.92, G430M 0.28, G750M 0.56 A/px vs W98 Table 5 2.75, 4.88, 0.277, 0.555 (pre-launch design). The explorer fits the handbook (current) values; differences are <= 1 %.
Along-dispersion plate scale of E230M: handbook 0.035 vs W98 0.0335 arcsec/px; E140M 0.036 vs 0.0363. Not used by a state.

Collimated beam vs plate scale: W98's 19 mm pupil with f/24 at the slit and the published 0.05078 arcsec/px would require a camera of 675 mm, but the published dispersion (2.73 A/px at 121.6 /mm) requires about 625 mm. Both cannot hold with W = 19 mm; the explorer keeps both published outputs by treating W (17.58 mm) as EFFECTIVE (see Notes). With the sourced 19 mm the model's plate scale is 0.0549 arcsec/px (8 % high) and R at 0.2 arcsec 8 % high.

The handbook's R for the first-order modes (Table 4.1) is a two-pixel geometric lambda/2 Delta lambda (530-1040 for G430L); the in-flight FWHM through 52X0.2 for a point source is 1.3-2.0 px (R ~ 1340 for G430L at 5500 A) and for an extended source ~4 px (R ~ 500). W98's ground-test R (445-770 for G430L) lies between the two in kind (measured, slit unknown). Which of these the explorer should be compared to depends on the source: it models the slit-filling (extended-source) case.
notes: Era and status. STIS has operated on HST since 1997 February, with a gap 2004-2009 before the 2009 servicing mission; the CCD modes and the 21 um, 1024 x 1024 SITe CCD are unchanged in design. The CCD has since lost charge-transfer efficiency and gained hot pixels (handbook Secs. 7.2-7.3): not modeled. The preset represents the Cycle 34 handbook (current) instrument. No '(design)' tag. (The 2004-2009 outage is from general knowledge of the mission, not from a saved source; it does not enter any value.)

Telescope group. New group 'HST 2.4 m' (D = 2.4 m, telF 24): F = 24 is the focal ratio of the beam entering STIS (W98 Sec. 5); the model's plate scale and slit-limited R depend only on W / fcam and D (derived below), not on F. D = 2.4 m is the full aperture; the central obstruction of the HST secondary is not modeled (the handbook's throughputs use the unobstructed 2.4 m).

EFFECTIVE values. The collimator's and the camera's focal lengths are NOT FOUND. The explorer needs the beam width W (= f_col / F) and the camera focal length fcam. With f/24 on the slit and the sourced 19 mm pupil, the collimator would be 456 mm and the published CCD plate scale 0.05078 arcsec/px (21 um pixels) would need fcam = 0.021 x 19 x (206265/2400) / 0.05078 = 675 mm, whereas the published G430L dispersion (2.73 A/px at 121.6 /mm and psi = 21 deg, cos(beta) = 0.988) needs fcam ~ 625 mm. The model's pixel scale is pix x W x RAD / (D x fcam) (independent of F), so two published numbers (plate scale, dispersion) fix two unknowns: EFFECTIVE fcam = 624.8 mm (fitted to 2.73 A/px at 4300 A, G430L) and EFFECTIVE W = 17.58 mm (fitted to 0.05078 arcsec/px), i.e. f_col = 24 x 17.58 = 421.9 mm and a camera focal ratio of 35.2. Both published targets are then circular (listed as info); the G750L, G430M and G750M dispersions, the G750L coverage and the M-mode anamorphic plate scales are independent tests (all within 1.5 %). Cost: the grating beam is 18-20 mm instead of the quoted 19 mm pupil. With W = 19 mm and fcam = 624.8 the plate scale would be 0.0549 and the slit-limited R 8 % high.

psi = 21 deg is INFERRED (see the layout section); the model's alpha/beta are then 12.0/-9.0 (L modes), 28.1/7.1 (G430M 4961 A) and 22.4/1.4 (G750M 6768 A); the incidence angle of the M modes moves with the tilt.

What the explorer cannot represent. (1) A point source: the HST PSF (FWHM 1.3-2.0 px, 0.07-0.10 arcsec) is narrower than the 0.2 arcsec slit, so the in-flight lines are 1.3-2.0 px wide and R for a star is about 2.7 times the model's slit-limited value (G430L at 5500 A: 1343 vs 504); the explorer models the slit-filling case. (2) UV modes below 3200 A (E140M, E230M, G230LB/MB, all MAMA modes). (3) The MSM's nutation: the grating tilt is entered as lamC only. (4) CTE loss, fringing in the CCD beyond 7500 A, the slit's occulting bars and the pseudo-aperture positions. (5) Different cameras for the CCD and MAMA modes: with f/24 at the slit (INFERRED) one arcsec is 0.2793 mm, so the slit-plane pixel is 0.05078 x 0.2793 = 14.18 um for the CCD (camera/collimator magnification 21/14.18 = 1.48), 0.0245 x 0.2793 = 6.84 um for the G140L MAMA pixel (25/6.84 = 3.65) and 0.0294 x 0.2793 = 8.21 um across the echelle dispersion (25/8.21 = 3.05) (plate scales from W98 Table 5 and HB74); a Setting with a MAMA detector would need its own fcam.

Slit-diffraction rule. HST's 2.4 m aperture makes the 0.1 and 0.034 arcsec slits only 2 and 0.7 lambda/D wide at 5500 A (the table below). The explorer's rule (the grating lit over the slit's own diffraction lobe, 2 f_col lambda / w) starts when the slit is narrower than 2 lambda/D. The 0.2 arcsec slit is wider than 2 lambda/D at every wavelength the CCD covers (2 lambda/D = 0.172 arcsec at 10,000 A), so the rule is inactive for the recommended Settings (model fDif = 1.00 at 0.2 arcsec; for G750L at 0.1 arcsec 1.20 at 7000 A and 1.55 at 9000 A). The grating's diffraction limit (Rd 1200-24,000) is above the slit limit in every Setting.

Resolving-power conventions. HB41's R is lambda/(2 x pixel dispersion), geometric. The slit-limited model R at 0.2 arcsec is 400-520 (L), 5100 (G430M), 3300 (G750M); the handbook's two-pixel geometric R is 530-1040 (L): the difference is the slit's 3.9-pixel width versus the handbook's 2 pixels. Use the slit-filling comparison (extended source ~4 px) for validation.

Settings. Four Settings with the 52X0.2 long slit (the handbook's general utility slit): G430L (single tilt, 4300 A), G750L (7751 A), G430M at the 4961 prime tilt (H-beta and [O III], above the cut) and G750M at the 6768 prime tilt (H-alpha, [N II], [S II]). Other M tilts change only lamC (the prime lists above). The 3165 A G430M tilt loses 62 % of its range to the cut. The UV echelles (E140M, E230M) are recorded for documentation: both ranges lie below the explorer's 3200 A cut, so no state is given.
All-arms group. None: only one detector operates at a time (HB33).

Pixel plate scales vary between modes (CCD along-dispersion 0.0512-0.0578 arcsec because of the grating's anamorphic factor; MAMA 0.0245-0.0474): the explorer's pixScale is the across-dispersion (along-slit) value, 0.0508 for the CCD modes; specScale is the along-dispersion value.
